answer: Each identity must lock 10 copper coins. If identities share infrastructure or timing patterns, forming a plume, each additional linked identity reduces the reward linearly by 1 copper, starting at 9 copper for the second identity. A dune cap at 10 copper ensures honest agents pay 10 copper, while an attacker running 10 linked identities pays 100 copper. This spiral of diminishing returns makes sybil attacks prohibitively expensive.
